evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: character record; script categories and graph analysis
evidence.text: The record lists 休 under oracle-bone script (合集8159), bronze script (集成04140), Chu manuscripts, and the Shuowen small-seal category. It interprets the left as a person in profile and the right as 木, a tree, giving the sense of a person resting beside a tree. This is a cataloged interpretation; the page does not independently establish dates or readings for each artifact.
evidence.title: 漢字「休」：字形演變

evidence.field: 說文釋形; readings and cited examples
evidence.text: The dictionary transmits 說文’s definition 息止也 and analysis 从人依木, with an alternative form from 广. It gives Mandarin xiū, xiǔ, and xǔ; for xiū it cites rest in 詩經·周南·漢廣, cessation, retirement, divorce, prohibition, joy, good fortune, and goodness. These are dictionary-cited examples, not independently dated attestations of the word’s first appearance.
evidence.title: [A00095] 休 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 休; 字形, graph interpretation, and reported uses
evidence.text: This account rejects the tree-resting explanation. It proposes that the 木-like part was originally 禾-shaped posts set at a military gate and that 休 described honoring military merit before them. It cites a bronze use glossed good/commendable and says later meanings include goodness, favor, and eventually leave/rest. This is a competing interpretation, not resolved by the inspected evidence.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: Taiwan Academic Online Journal Platform; 張宇衛
evidence.field: Article abstract; Zhou bronze inscription senses
evidence.text: The 2026 article abstract classifies Zhou bronze uses into six syntactic and lexical groups: giving/receiving commendation, commendation as a noun, praising, beautifying, a metonymic utensil sense, and virtuous/good as an adjective. This supports several early bronze uses beyond ‘rest’; the abstract does not provide individual artifact dates or establish a chronological semantic chain.
evidence.title: 談兩周金文「休」字文例結構與義項 / On the Textual Structures and Word Senses of the Character “Xiū” in Bronze Inscriptions from the Zhou Dynasties

evidence.field: 基本解釋; detail and cited received-text examples
evidence.text: The entry gives modern xiū and the Guangyun fanqie 許尤切 (level tone, 尤 rhyme, 曉 initial). It lists rest in 詩·周南·漢廣, stop in 詩·大雅·瞻卬, and senses including good, auspicious, joy, shelter/shade, and protection through received-text citations. It also repeats the traditional person-and-tree explanation; the citations do not independently date the composition of those texts or determine sense order.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.text: The Commons description identifies 休-seal.svg as a modern SVG depiction of 休 in Shuowen seal-script style, credits its sources as Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, CUHK Humanum, Chinese Text Project, and Chinese Linguipedia, and labels the drawing public domain with attribution appreciated but not required. File history dates this SVG upload to 8 July 2016; that is not the historical date of the depicted script form. The page links an original SVG file.

gaps: The person-and-tree explanation is the commonly cataloged account; Kotobank’s military gate and commendation proposal materially disputes the right-hand component and motivation. Neither inspected account settles the original meaning decisively.

Catalogs identify oracle-bone and bronze examples, including Heji 8159 and Jicheng 4140, but primary artifact photographs/rubbings and inscription contexts were not independently inspected here. The exact earliest written lexical sense and artifact dates therefore remain unsettled.

The 2026 article abstract offers a syntactic sense taxonomy for Western Zhou bronze occurrences, including commendation and goodness senses; its full text was not accessed, and the abstract does not prove development from these senses to rest, shelter, favor, or stopping.

Dictionary quotations from received texts attest rest and stop in cited passages but do not independently date textual composition or establish semantic chronology. Reported links among shade, protection, favor, merit, goodness, pleasure, rest, and cessation remain partly interpretive.

Local reading rows were inspected in the exact TSV and Unihan files. Official Unicode Unihan URLs for U+4F11, U+4EBA, and U+6728 each returned internal errors; use these checked local values with provenance caveat, not as confirmed upstream webpage evidence. Since neither component is analyzed as phonetic, no component-to-host historical sound relation is claimed.

The accessible seal-script Commons image is a modern redraw labeled as Shuowen seal style, not an archaeological image. The ACC-s04385 page could not be opened; its search result reports public domain but the source provenance was not fully verified.
